transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

I cannot confirm what ER03 specifically means on your AEG model as it is not in my standard error catalogue, so we will focus on the symptom of it switching off after the boil-over. The most likely cause here is moisture or pasta water tracking under the control panel, which can trigger a safety shutdown to protect the electronics. Please switch the hob off at the consumer unit and leave it completely dry for at least 24 hours before trying again. If you smell burning plastic or see scorch marks, stop using it immediately as this indicates an electrical fault.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
No burning smell or scorch marks. I've already wiped it dry and switched it off at the wall for 5 minutes, and it works again now. Is that enough or do I really need to leave it 24 hours?

Since it has reset after five minutes, you likely just need to ensure the control panel area is completely dry rather than waiting a full 24 hours. You can leave the power on for now but keep an eye on it to make sure the error does not return immediately. To stop this happening again, try to use larger pans so they do not overflow as easily during boiling. If the hob starts beeping or showing Er03 again, switch it off at the wall and let it dry out thoroughly before trying once more. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make AEG; model IKB64301FB; code ER03.
The fault they reported is: "keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
They asked: "Is that enough or do I really need to leave it 24 hours?" - answer that first.
The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.
